t: #3907 Count Smaller Elements With Opposite Parity — Fenwick Tree Sweep
o: For each index i, count later indices j with nums[j] < nums[i] and opposite parity — a 'count smaller to the right' problem with a parity twist. Sweep right to left, keeping two Fenwick trees (one for even values seen, one for odd); before inserting nums[i], query the opposite-parity tree for values strictly below it. Coordinate-compress values since they reach 1e9. Example [5,2,4,1,3] gives [2,1,2,0,0].
k: Right-to-left sweep with 'insert after query' turns suffix counting into prefix counting.
Two Fenwick trees (even/odd) over compressed values answer opposite-parity smaller-count queries in O(log n).
Strict inequality means query the prefix count below rank(nums[i]), i.e., rank - 1 elements.

a.i: For each i, scan all j > i and count matches. O(n^2) — fine conceptually, too slow for n = 1e5, but the natural baseline.
s: For each i, initialize a counter.
For each j > i, if nums[j] < nums[i] and parities differ, increment.

a.n: Approach 2: Two Fenwick trees over compressed values
a.i: Traverse from the right. For index i, the count of already-seen (i.e., to-the-right) opposite-parity values smaller than nums[i] is a prefix query on the corresponding tree; then insert nums[i] into its own parity tree.
s: Maintain Fenwick trees bitE (evens) and bitO (odds), initially empty.
For i from n-1 down to 0: query the opposite-parity tree for prefix sum at rank(nums[i]) - 1; record it; then add 1 at rank(nums[i]) in nums[i]'s parity tree.
a.t: O(n log n) — compression sort plus two Fenwick operations per element.
a.sp: O(n) for the trees and rank table.

w: This is the classic 'count inversions by parity class' pattern; a merge-sort based alternative also works but Fenwick trees adapt more easily to the parity split. Pitfalls: using <= instead of < (query rank - 1 for strictness), inserting before querying (would count the element itself), and forgetting duplicates compress to one rank. Follow-up: count smaller-or-equal same-parity elements, or answer the queries online for streaming inserts.
